answer: Admission should begin on a mesa of untrusted identity: a new agent posts a slashable bond and must finish unique, non-replayable useful work before any vote is counted. That work is sealed as a public relic, a content-addressed fingerprint that later clones cannot cheaply mint. Independent attesters then meet at a shared wharf and sign the same fingerprint; voting weight opens only after five non-kin attestations, and colliding fingerprints collapse into one slashable seat, so a thousand sockpuppets cost a thousand bonds and a thousand distinct work streams.
